categories.desc: Little words that make people look, listen or wait.
cards: Dis donc !
Hey! / Wow!
Gets attention or shows mild surprise. Formal or plural: dites donc ! Also a reproach: dis donc, tu pourrais dire merci !
Dis donc, ils ont mis le paquet pour la déco !
Wow, they've really gone all out on the decorations!
Tiens !
Well, look! / Here!
Surprise (tiens, il pleut), or handing something over (tiens, c'est pour toi). Formal: tenez.
Tiens, regarde qui voilà !
Well, look who's here!
Attends !
Hang on! / Wait!
Stops someone, or signals a realisation or correction. Formal: attendez !
Attends, il en reste encore dans le frigo.
Hang on, there's still some left in the fridge.
Écoute…
Look… / Listen…
Opens something serious or a firm point. Formal: écoutez…
Écoute, je n'ai pas le temps de discuter.
Look, I don't have time to argue.
Regarde !
Look!
Points something out. Also, like écoute, before a firm point: regarde, c'est simple.
Regarde, il y a un écureuil sur la branche !
Look, there's a squirrel on the branch!
Bah alors ?
Hey, what's going on? / Come on!
When something seems wrong or needs a little scolding. Very casual.
Bah alors, qu'est-ce que tu fais encore en pyjama ?
Come on, what are you doing still in your pyjamas?
Eh ben alors ?
Hey, what's wrong?
Softer and more caring than bah alors. Often to a child who's upset.
Eh ben alors, qu'est-ce qu'il y a, mon cœur ?
Hey, what's the matter, sweetheart?
Et alors ?
So what?
Challenges or dismisses what was just said. Also as a genuine ‘and then?’ in a story.
— Il n'aime pas ton idée. — Et alors ?
— He doesn't like your idea. — So what?
Quand même !
Honestly! / Come on!
Indignation or insistence: c'est cher, quand même ! At the end of a sentence it also means ‘still, all the same’.
Tu aurais pu prévenir, quand même !
Honestly, you could have warned me!
Bon…
Right… / OK then…
Announces a decision, a change of topic or the end of a chat. Bon ben… : well then…
Bon, on y va ?
Right, shall we go?
Ouais.
Yeah.
Informal oui. Sceptical, drawn out: ouais, ouais… (yeah, right…)
— Tu viens ce soir ? — Ouais, je pense.
— Are you coming tonight? — Yeah, I think so.

categories.desc: Changing topic, adding a thought, checking in.
cards: Tu sais…
You know…
Softens what follows and draws the listener in. Formal: vous savez…
Tu sais, il ne me demande jamais rien.
You know, he never asks me for anything.
Au fait, …
By the way, …
Brings up something new. The t is pronounced: o fèt. Also à propos, … (by the way).
Au fait, Jacques m'a appelée hier.
By the way, Jacques called me yesterday.
En parlant de ça, …
Speaking of which, …
Links to what was just said. Also à propos de ça.
En parlant de ça, tu as vu le nouveau film d'Ozon ?
Speaking of which, have you seen the new Ozon film?
…, non ?
…, right? / …, isn't it?
Tacked on to ask for agreement: c'est joli, non ? Also …, hein ? (more casual) or …, c'est ça ?
Il fait beau aujourd'hui, non ?
It's lovely today, isn't it?
En vrai, …
Honestly, … / Actually, …
Young and casual: to be honest, really. Also as a question: en vrai ? (seriously?)
En vrai, t'as raison, on devrait partir plus tôt.
Honestly, you're right, we should leave earlier.
En tout cas, …
Anyway, … / In any case, …
Wraps up or moves on, whatever else is true.
En tout cas, tu gardes ça pour toi.
In any case, you keep this to yourself.
Effectivement.
Indeed. / That's right.
Confirms what someone said. Also en effet (more formal).
— Le magasin ferme à midi le samedi ? — Effectivement.
— Does the shop close at noon on Saturdays? — That's right.
